items.headline: Supreme Court upholds demonetisation
items.detail: The Supreme Court upheld by majority the legality of the government's November 2016 decision demonetising Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes, dismissing dozens of petitions challenging it.

items.headline: CCI rejects Google's appeal in Android antitrust case
items.detail: The Competition Commission of India rejected Google's appeal against its October 2022 ruling that the company's dominance in search and the Android app store breached antitrust law.

items.headline: Bolsonaro supporters storm Brasilia buildings
items.detail: A week after Lula da Silva's inauguration, thousands of supporters of ex-president Jair Bolsonaro stormed Brazil's National Congress, Supreme Federal Court and the Planalto presidential palace in Brasilia on January 8, 2023; police retook the buildings the same day.

items.headline: Odisha hosts the Men's Hockey World Cup
items.detail: India hosted the 15th Men's FIH Hockey World Cup from January 13-29, 2023 across Bhubaneswar and Rourkela, with the new Birsa Munda Stadium in Rourkela among the venues.

items.headline: Djokovic wins a 10th Australian Open
items.detail: Novak Djokovic beat Stefanos Tsitsipas in the Australian Open final (January 16-29, 2023) for a record 10th Melbourne title and 22nd Grand Slam, tying Rafael Nadal's all-time mark. Aryna Sabalenka won her first major, beating Elena Rybakina.
examFacts: Men: Djokovic beat Tsitsipas (10th AO, 22nd Slam)

items.headline: Top wrestlers protest against WFI chief
items.detail: Bajrang Punia, Vinesh Phogat and Sakshi Malik began a protest at Jantar Mantar on January 18, 2023, with Phogat accusing WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh of sexual harassment - the start of months-long demonstrations.

items.headline: Hindenburg report triggers Adani rout
items.detail: US short-seller Hindenburg Research alleged on January 24, 2023 that the Adani Group ran 'a brazen stock manipulation and accounting fraud scheme'. Group stocks crashed about $150 billion in value by end-February, and Gautam Adani fell from the world's third-richest person to 30th in a month.

items.headline: 74th Republic Day with Egypt's President as chief guest
items.detail: India celebrated its 74th Republic Day on January 26, 2023, with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi as chief guest at the parade.

items.headline: India lift inaugural U-19 Women's T20 World Cup
items.detail: India beat England by seven wickets in the final at Potchefstroom, South Africa on January 29, 2023 to win the first ICC Under-19 Women's T20 World Cup. England's Grace Scrivens was Player of the Tournament; India's Shweta Sehrawat was the top run-scorer with 297.

items.headline: Germany win the Hockey World Cup
items.detail: Germany beat defending champions Belgium 5-4 in a shootout after a 3-3 final at the Men's FIH Hockey World Cup on January 29, 2023 for a third title. Niklas Wellen was named best player; the Netherlands took bronze.
examFacts: Player of the Tournament: Niklas Wellen

quiz.q: On January 2, 2023, the Supreme Court upheld the legality of:
quiz.solution: The Court dismissed challenges to the November 2016 demonetisation by a majority.

quiz.q: The January 8, 2023 riots in Brasilia targeted all EXCEPT which building?
quiz.solution: Congress, the Supreme Court and the Planalto were stormed; the Alvorada (residence) was not.

quiz.q: How many Grand Slam titles did Djokovic tie Nadal's record with at the 2023 Australian Open?
quiz.solution: His 10th Australian Open title was his 22nd major, equalling Nadal.

quiz.q: Who won the inaugural ICC U-19 Women's T20 World Cup in January 2023?
quiz.solution: India beat England by seven wickets at Potchefstroom on January 29, 2023.

quiz.q: Which country won the 2023 Men's FIH Hockey World Cup hosted by India?
quiz.solution: Germany beat Belgium 5-4 in a shootout after a 3-3 final for a third title.

quiz.q: The Hindenburg Research report on the Adani Group was released on:
quiz.solution: The January 24 report triggered an eventual ~\$150 billion wipeout in group value.

quiz.q: Who was the chief guest at India's 74th Republic Day parade in 2023?
quiz.solution: Egypt's President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi attended on January 26, 2023.

quiz.q: Where did the first women wrestlers' protest against the WFI chief begin in January 2023?
quiz.solution: Bajrang Punia, Vinesh Phogat and Sakshi Malik began the sit-in at Jantar Mantar on January 18.

quiz.q: Aryna Sabalenka's 2023 Australian Open win was her:
quiz.solution: She beat Elena Rybakina for a maiden major.

quiz.q: Which Indian city co-hosted the 2023 Hockey World Cup alongside Bhubaneswar?
quiz.solution: The Birsa Munda Stadium in Rourkela hosted matches alongside the Kalinga Stadium.

items.headline: Union Budget 2023-24 presented
items.detail: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget 2023-24 on February 1, 2023 - the fourth of the NDA's second term - calling it the first budget of 'Amrit Kaal'. Total expenditure was Rs 45.03 lakh crore with the fiscal deficit pegged at 5.9% of GDP and revised slabs under the new income tax regime.

items.headline: US shoots down Chinese surveillance balloon
items.detail: An F-22 Raptor shot down a Chinese high-altitude balloon off the US East Coast on February 4, 2023, on President Biden's orders - the first aircraft downed over the United States since World War II - escalating tensions with Beijing.
examFacts: By an F-22 over the Atlantic

items.headline: Turkey-Syria earthquakes kill tens of thousands
items.detail: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck near Gaziantep in southern Turkey at dawn on February 6, 2023, followed hours later by a magnitude 7.7 near Kahramanmaras. The quakes and aftershocks - including a 6.3 on February 20 - killed an estimated 59,000-62,000 people across Turkey and Syria, the deadliest disaster in modern Turkish history.

items.headline: India take 2-0 lead in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy
items.detail: India won the first two Tests of the 2023 Border-Gavaskar Trophy - by an innings and 132 runs at Nagpur (February 9-13) and by six wickets at Delhi (February 17-21) - both inside three days, putting Australia's World Test Championship final hopes in jeopardy.

items.headline: Tinubu wins Nigeria's presidential election
items.detail: Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress won Nigeria's February 25, 2023 presidential election with 36.61% of the vote, ahead of Atiku Abubakar (PDP, 29.07%) and Peter Obi (Labour, 25.40%), in a poll with record-low 26.71% turnout.

items.headline: Delhi ministers Sisodia and Jain resign after arrests
items.detail: Delhi Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia and Health Minister Satyendra Jain resigned from the Arvind Kejriwal cabinet on February 28, 2023 following their arrests - Sisodia by the CBI in the liquor policy case on February 26 and Jain earlier by the ED.

items.headline: Greece's deadliest rail disaster
items.detail: A passenger train and a freight train collided head-on in the Tempi valley in northern Greece on the night of February 28, 2023, killing 57 people - Greece's deadliest rail disaster - after the Larissa stationmaster routed the train onto the wrong track.

items.headline: India eye series win over Australia
items.detail: India ended February with a 2-0 lead over Australia in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy, with the third Test at Indore starting March 1 and the finale at Ahmedabad to follow; India sealed the series 2-1 in March, with Ashwin and Jadeja named Players of the Series.
examFacts: Players of the Series: Ashwin and Jadeja

quiz.q: The Union Budget 2023-24 was presented on:
quiz.solution: Nirmala Sitharaman presented the fourth budget of the NDA's second term on February 1, 2023.

quiz.q: The Union Budget 2023-24 pegged the fiscal deficit at what percentage of GDP?
quiz.solution: The deficit was set at 5.9%, with expenditure of Rs 45.03 lakh crore.

quiz.q: The February 6, 2023 earthquake that devastated Turkey and Syria measured:
quiz.solution: The M7.8 quake near Gaziantep was followed hours later by an M7.7 near Kahramanmaras.

quiz.q: Which aircraft shot down the Chinese balloon over the Atlantic on February 4, 2023?
quiz.solution: An F-22 Raptor downed it on Biden's orders - the first such shootdown over the US since WWII.

quiz.q: Who won Nigeria's February 2023 presidential election?
quiz.solution: Tinubu (APC) polled 36.61% against Atiku's 29.07% and Obi's 25.40%.

quiz.q: Manish Sisodia resigned as Delhi Deputy CM in February 2023 after arrest by:
quiz.solution: The CBI arrested him on February 26 in the liquor policy case; he resigned on February 28.

quiz.q: Greece's deadliest rail disaster, with 57 deaths, occurred in the:
quiz.solution: The February 28, 2023 head-on crash near Tempi followed wrong-track routing by a stationmaster.

quiz.q: India won the first Test of the 2023 Border-Gavaskar Trophy at Nagpur by:
quiz.solution: India then won the Delhi Test by six wickets for a 2-0 lead.

quiz.q: India's final series result against Australia in the 2023 Border-Gavaskar Trophy was:
quiz.solution: Australia's Indore win and the Ahmedabad draw left India 2-1 winners; both teams made the WTC final.

quiz.q: Who were named joint Players of the Series in the 2023 Border-Gavaskar Trophy?
quiz.solution: Ashwin topped the wicket charts with 25 as India retained the trophy.

items.headline: BJP retains Tripura and Nagaland; Meghalaya hung
items.detail: Assembly election results declared on March 2, 2023 saw the BJP retain Tripura and Nagaland, while Meghalaya returned a hung assembly.

items.headline: Inaugural Women's Premier League begins
items.detail: The first Women's Premier League T20 season opened on March 4, 2023 with five franchises - Delhi Capitals, Gujarat Giants, Mumbai Indians, Royal Challengers Bangalore and UP Warriorz - playing in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai until March 26.
examFacts: Venues: Brabourne and DY Patil Stadiums

items.headline: Silicon Valley Bank collapses
items.detail: California regulators seized Silicon Valley Bank on March 10, 2023 after a bank run saw customers pull $42 billion in a day - the largest US bank failure since 2008. Signature Bank was closed on March 12; all depositors got access to funds by March 13.

items.headline: ICC issues arrest warrant for Vladimir Putin
items.detail: The International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants on March 17, 2023 for President Vladimir Putin and Russia's children's rights commissioner Maria Lvova-Belova over the alleged deportation and forced adoption of Ukrainian children.

items.headline: Punjab cracks down on Waris Punjab De
items.detail: Punjab Police launched a crackdown on the organisation Waris Punjab De led by Khalistan separatist Amritpal Singh on March 18, 2023, arresting 78 people initially; Singh was captured weeks later.

items.headline: UBS buys crisis-hit Credit Suisse
items.detail: UBS agreed on March 19, 2023 to take over its ailing rival Credit Suisse with Swiss government backing, as the 167-year-old bank faced imminent insolvency during a global banking scare.

items.headline: Rahul Gandhi disqualified from Lok Sabha
items.detail: Rahul Gandhi was disqualified as a Lok Sabha member after a Surat court convicted him of defamation on March 23, 2023 and sentenced him to two years in jail over 'Modi surname' remarks; his Wayanad seat was declared vacant the next day.

items.headline: Mumbai Indians win inaugural WPL title
items.detail: Mumbai Indians beat Delhi Capitals by seven wickets in the first Women's Premier League final on March 26, 2023. Nat Sciver-Brunt's unbeaten 60 sealed the chase; Hayley Matthews was Player of the Series (16 wickets) and Meg Lanning took the Orange Cap with 345 runs.

items.headline: IPL 2023 season gets underway
items.detail: The IPL 2023 season began on March 31, 2023 and ran to May 30, returning to home-and-away venues after three years, with the Gujarat Titans defending their title.

quiz.q: Silicon Valley Bank was seized by regulators on which date in March 2023?
quiz.solution: A \$42 billion bank run led to its seizure on March 10 - the largest US bank failure since 2008.

quiz.q: The ICC arrest warrant of March 17, 2023 against Vladimir Putin concerns:
quiz.solution: Putin and children's commissioner Maria Lvova-Belova face charges over deportation of children.

quiz.q: Which bank agreed to take over Credit Suisse on March 19, 2023?
quiz.solution: UBS's government-backed rescue came as Credit Suisse faced insolvency.

quiz.q: Rahul Gandhi was disqualified from the Lok Sabha after a court in which city sentenced him?
quiz.solution: A Surat court gave him two years for defamation over 'Modi surname' remarks.

quiz.q: Which team won the inaugural Women's Premier League in March 2023?
quiz.solution: MI beat DC by 7 wickets in the March 26 final; Nat Sciver-Brunt hit 60*.

quiz.q: Who was Player of the Series in the first WPL season?
quiz.solution: Matthews took 16 wickets - the most - for champions Mumbai Indians.

quiz.q: In the March 2023 northeast assembly results, the BJP retained:
quiz.solution: Meghalaya returned a hung assembly; BJP kept Tripura and Nagaland.

quiz.q: Amritpal Singh, targeted in the March 2023 Punjab crackdown, led which organisation?
quiz.solution: Punjab Police acted against Waris Punjab De on March 18, 2023, arresting 78 people initially.

quiz.q: The IPL 2023 season began on:
quiz.solution: It ran March 31 to May 30, 2023, returning to home-and-away venues.

quiz.q: Who was charged alongside Putin in the ICC warrants?
quiz.solution: Russia's children's rights commissioner was named for the same deportation allegations.

items.headline: UN projects India as the world's most populous country
items.detail: In April 2023, the UN Population Fund projected that India would overtake China as the world's most populous country by mid-2023, with roughly 1.4 billion people in each country at the crossover.

items.headline: New income tax law comes into force
items.detail: A new income tax law took effect in India on April 1, 2023, replacing the 1961 statute, including a disputed 'angel tax' provision aimed at taxing foreign money flowing into Indian start-ups.

items.headline: Finland joins NATO as its 31st member
items.detail: Finland became NATO's 31st member on April 4, 2023 after all 30 allies ratified its accession, ending decades of military non-alignment triggered by Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

items.headline: ESA launches JUICE to Jupiter's icy moons
items.detail: The European Space Agency launched JUICE (Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer) on an Ariane 5 from Kourou on April 14, 2023 to study Ganymede, Callisto and Europa. It arrives at Jupiter in July 2031 and will become the first spacecraft to orbit a moon other than Earth's - Ganymede - in 2034.

items.headline: Civil war erupts in Sudan
items.detail: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces under Gen. Hemedti attacked army bases on April 15, 2023, sparking all-out war with the SAF of Gen. al-Burhan over the RSF's integration. Khartoum became a battleground and India launched Operation Kaveri to evacuate citizens.

items.headline: Deadly Asian heat wave smashes records
items.detail: An April 2023 heat wave brought deaths and school closures in India, with Thailand recording 44.6 degrees Celsius at Tak and Laos 42.7 at Luang Prabang - national records.

items.headline: Wrestlers resume protest against WFI chief
items.detail: Top wrestlers including Bajrang Punia, Sakshi Malik and Vinesh Phogat resumed their protest at Jantar Mantar on April 23, 2023, demanding the arrest of WFI president Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh over sexual harassment allegations after the oversight committee's report was withheld.

items.headline: Two FIRs filed against Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh
items.detail: Under Supreme Court pressure, Delhi Police registered two FIRs against WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on April 28, 2023 - one under the POCSO Act and one for outraging the modesty of women wrestlers.

items.headline: Ding Liren becomes 17th World Chess Champion
items.detail: China's Ding Liren defeated Ian Nepomniachtchi in rapid tiebreaks on April 30, 2023 to win the World Chess Championship, becoming the 17th champion after Magnus Carlsen declined to defend his title.

quiz.q: Finland became which numbered member of NATO in April 2023?
quiz.solution: Finland joined on April 4, 2023 after all 30 allies ratified; Sweden followed in March 2024.

quiz.q: ESA's JUICE mission, launched April 14, 2023, will be the first spacecraft to:
options: Orbit a moon other than Earth's
quiz.solution: JUICE will orbit Ganymede from 2034 after reaching Jupiter in July 2031.

quiz.q: The Sudan civil war that began on April 15, 2023 pits the SAF under al-Burhan against:
quiz.solution: The Rapid Support Forces' integration into the army was the core dispute.

quiz.q: India's evacuation mission for citizens caught in the Sudan war was named:
quiz.solution: Operation Kaveri brought Indians home from Sudan after fighting began April 15, 2023.

quiz.q: Which UN agency projected in April 2023 that India would overtake China in population by mid-2023?
quiz.solution: The UN Population Fund made the projection as India neared 1.4 billion people.

quiz.q: The wrestlers' protest of April 2023 demanded the arrest of which WFI chief?
quiz.solution: Protests resumed at Jantar Mantar on April 23 over sexual harassment allegations.

quiz.q: Under Supreme Court pressure on April 28, 2023, Delhi Police filed FIRs against Brij Bhushan including one under:
quiz.solution: Two FIRs were registered - one POCSO (a minor complainant) and one for outraging modesty.

quiz.q: Ding Liren became the ___ World Chess Champion by beating Ian Nepomniachtchi in 2023.
quiz.solution: He won in rapid tiebreaks on April 30, 2023 after Magnus Carlsen declined to defend.

quiz.q: The April 2023 heat wave set a Thai record of 44.6 degrees Celsius at:
quiz.solution: Laos (42.7 C at Luang Prabang) also recorded a national high.

quiz.q: India's new income tax law effective April 1, 2023 replaced the statute of which year?
quiz.solution: The 1961 Act was replaced, with a contested angel-tax provision for start-ups.

items.headline: Ethnic violence erupts in Manipur
items.detail: Clashes between the Meitei and Kuki communities broke out in Manipur on May 3, 2023 after a 'Tribal Solidarity March', killing at least 73 people initially and displacing tens of thousands in an ethnic conflict that simmered for months.

items.headline: WHO ends COVID-19 global health emergency
items.detail: The World Health Organization declared on May 5, 2023 that COVID-19 was no longer a global health emergency - more than three years after first designating it in January 2020 - while reclassifying it as an ongoing global health threat.

items.headline: King Charles III crowned at Westminster Abbey
items.detail: Charles III was crowned at Westminster Abbey on May 6, 2023 alongside Queen Camilla - the first British coronation in 70 years, since Elizabeth II's in June 1953, and the first of the 21st century.

items.headline: Congress wins Karnataka
items.detail: The Congress won the Karnataka assembly election, taking 135 of 224 seats and unseating the BJP; results were declared on May 13 after polling on May 10, with Siddaramaiah returning as chief minister.

items.headline: Cyclone Mocha devastates Myanmar's Rakhine coast
items.detail: Cyclone Mocha, an extremely severe cyclonic storm, made landfall just north of Sittwe in Myanmar's Rakhine State on May 14, 2023, killing between 145 and 463 people by varying counts, many of them Rohingya.

items.headline: RBI withdraws the Rs 2,000 note
items.detail: The RBI announced on May 19, 2023 the withdrawal of the Rs 2,000 banknote from circulation under its Clean Note Policy, setting a September 2023 deadline that was later extended to October 7; the notes remained legal tender.

items.headline: G7 leaders meet in Hiroshima
items.detail: The 49th G7 Summit was held in Hiroshima, Japan on May 19-21, 2023, chaired by PM Fumio Kishida. Ukraine's Zelenskyy attended in person; leaders issued the 'Hiroshima Vision on Nuclear Disarmament' and launched the Hiroshima AI process. PM Modi was among eight outreach invitees.

items.headline: Tina Turner, 'Queen of Rock 'n' Roll', dies
items.detail: Tina Turner died in Kusnacht, Switzerland on May 24, 2023, aged 83. The 12-time Grammy winner, with hits like 'What's Love Got to Do with It' and 'Proud Mary', sold over 100 million records and entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame twice.

items.headline: PM inaugurates the new Parliament building
items.detail: PM Modi inaugurated the new Parliament House on May 28, 2023, installing the historic Sengol sceptre near the Speaker's chair; the triangular building sits beside the existing Parliament House.

items.headline: Erdogan re-elected Turkish president
items.detail: Recep Tayyip Erdogan won Turkey's presidential runoff on May 28, 2023 with 52.18% against Kemal Kilicdaroglu's 47.82%, securing a third presidential term in a poll held alongside parliamentary elections.

items.headline: CSK win a fifth IPL title in a rain-hit final
items.detail: Chennai Super Kings beat Gujarat Titans by five wickets via the DLS method in the IPL 2023 final at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad on May 30, 2023, claiming a fifth title. Shubman Gill won the Orange Cap (890 runs) and was Most Valuable Player.

quiz.q: The new Parliament building of India was inaugurated on:
quiz.solution: PM Modi inaugurated it on May 28, 2023 and installed the Sengol near the Speaker's chair.

quiz.q: How many seats did the Congress win in the May 2023 Karnataka assembly election?
quiz.solution: The Congress won 135 of 224 seats, unseating the BJP.

quiz.q: The RBI announced the withdrawal of which banknote on May 19, 2023?
quiz.solution: Under the Clean Note Policy, Rs 2,000 notes were withdrawn but stayed legal tender.

quiz.q: Charles III's coronation in May 2023 was the first British coronation in:
quiz.solution: Elizabeth II was crowned in June 1953 - nearly 70 years earlier.

quiz.q: With what vote share did Erdogan win the May 2023 Turkish runoff?
quiz.solution: He beat Kilicdaroglu 52.18% to 47.82% for a third presidential term.

quiz.q: The 2023 IPL title was Chennai Super Kings':
quiz.solution: CSK beat GT by 5 wickets (DLS) in Ahmedabad for a fifth crown.

quiz.q: The 49th G7 Summit in May 2023 was hosted by which city?
quiz.solution: Hiroshima hosted under Japan's chairmanship; the 'Hiroshima Vision' on nuclear disarmament was issued.

quiz.q: Cyclone Mocha made landfall in May 2023 in which Myanmar state?
quiz.solution: It struck just north of Sittwe in Rakhine State on May 14, 2023.

quiz.q: Tina Turner, who died in May 2023, was known as the:
quiz.solution: The 12-time Grammy winner sold over 100 million records.

quiz.q: On May 5, 2023, the WHO declared that COVID-19 was no longer a:
quiz.solution: The emergency designation, in place since January 2020, was lifted; COVID remains a health threat.

items.headline: Odisha triple train collision kills over 280
items.detail: The Coromandel Express derailed near Bahanaga Bazar station in Balasore district, Odisha on June 2, 2023, colliding with a freight train and hitting another passenger train - India's deadliest rail disaster in decades, killing over 280 people.

items.headline: Kakhovka dam destroyed in occupied Ukraine
items.detail: The Kakhovka dam on the Dnieper in Russian-occupied Kherson Oblast was breached in the early hours of June 6, 2023, submerging about 600 sq km and flooding 24 villages; tens of thousands were affected and dozens died. Ukraine blamed Russia, which denied it.

items.headline: Australia beat India to win World Test Championship
items.detail: Australia beat India by 209 runs in the World Test Championship final at The Oval (June 7-11, 2023), with Travis Head's 163 earning him Player of the Match. It was Australia's maiden WTC title, making them the first team to win all ICC titles in all three formats.
examFacts: Player of the Match: Travis Head (163)

items.headline: Djokovic wins record 23rd major at French Open
items.detail: Novak Djokovic beat Casper Ruud in the French Open final on June 11, 2023, claiming the all-time record of 23 men's Grand Slam titles and passing Rafael Nadal's 22. Iga Swiatek won the women's title, beating Karolina Muchova.

items.headline: Heat wave deaths mount in UP and Bihar
items.detail: At least 96 deaths were linked to the June 17, 2023 heat wave in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, part of a brutal early-summer across northern India.

items.headline: Titan submersible implodes on Titanic dive
items.detail: The OceanGate submersible Titan lost contact 1 hour 33 minutes into a dive to the Titanic wreck on June 18, 2023; debris found on June 22 confirmed an implosion that killed all five aboard, including OceanGate CEO Stockton Rush.

items.headline: Khalistani separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar shot dead in Canada
items.detail: Hardeep Singh Nijjar - whom India accused of leading the Khalistan Tiger Force - was shot dead by masked gunmen in the parking lot of a Surrey, British Columbia gurdwara on June 18, 2023, an event that later triggered a major India-Canada row.

items.headline: Record June heat bakes Asia
items.detail: Beijing recorded 41 degrees Celsius on June 22, 2023 - its hottest June day since 1961 - while a heat wave in northern India killed at least 170 people with temperatures near 46 degrees.

items.headline: Wembanyama heads NBA Draft
items.detail: French prodigy Victor Wembanyama was selected first overall by the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Draft on June 22, 2023.

items.headline: Zambia restructures $6.3 billion Chinese debt
items.detail: Zambia agreed with the Export-Import Bank of China and other creditors to restructure US$6.3 billion of debt on June 22, 2023, a French-facilitated deal unlocking a $1.3 billion IMF bailout.

items.headline: Wagner mutiny: mercenaries march on Moscow
items.detail: Wagner Group chief Yevgeny Prigozhin seized Rostov-on-Don on June 23, 2023 and sent an armoured column toward Moscow in a 'march of justice' against Russia's military leadership. Belarusian President Lukashenko brokered a stand-down on June 24; rebellion charges were dropped on June 27.
examFacts: Prigozhin later died in an August 23 plane crash

quiz.q: The June 2023 Odisha triple train collision occurred near which station?
quiz.solution: The Coromandel Express derailed near Bahanaga Bazar in Balasore district, killing 280+.

quiz.q: Australia won the 2023 World Test Championship final at The Oval by:
quiz.solution: Travis Head's 163 won him Player of the Match in Australia's maiden WTC title.

quiz.q: Djokovic's 2023 French Open title was his record ___ men's Grand Slam.
quiz.solution: He passed Rafael Nadal's 22 by beating Casper Ruud in the June 11 final.

quiz.q: The Titan submersible that imploded in June 2023 was diving to which wreck?
quiz.solution: The OceanGate vessel imploded during a dive to the Titanic; all five aboard died.

quiz.q: Which city did Wagner fighters seize during the June 2023 mutiny?
quiz.solution: Wagner took Rostov-on-Don before Lukashenko brokered the June 24 stand-down.

quiz.q: The Kakhovka dam destroyed in June 2023 stood on which river?
quiz.solution: The dam on the Dnieper in Kherson Oblast was breached on June 6, 2023.

quiz.q: Hardeep Singh Nijjar, whose June 2023 killing sparked an India-Canada row, lived in:
quiz.solution: He was shot dead in Surrey, British Columbia on June 18, 2023.

quiz.q: Who was selected first overall in the 2023 NBA Draft?
quiz.solution: France's Wembanyama went first to the San Antonio Spurs on June 22, 2023.

quiz.q: Zambia's June 2023 debt restructuring deal with Chinese creditors totalled:
quiz.solution: The \$6.3 billion restructuring unlocked a \$1.3 billion IMF bailout.

quiz.q: Iga Swiatek beat which player in the 2023 French Open women's final?
quiz.solution: Swiatek beat Czech Karolina Muchova at Roland Garros.

items.headline: NCP splits as Ajit Pawar joins Maharashtra ruling alliance
items.detail: The Nationalist Congress Party split on July 2, 2023, when Ajit Pawar and several NCP leaders crossed over to the BJP-led Maha Yuti alliance in Maharashtra, deepening the state's political churn.
examFacts: Ajit Pawar joined the Maha Yuti

items.headline: Milan Kundera, author of 'The Unbearable Lightness of Being', dies
items.detail: Czech-French writer Milan Kundera, whose novel 'The Unbearable Lightness of Being' (1984) became a modern classic, died in Paris on July 11, 2023, aged 94. His books were banned in communist Czechoslovakia before the 1989 Velvet Revolution.

items.headline: NATO leaders meet in Vilnius
items.detail: NATO held its summit at Vilnius, Lithuania on July 11-12, 2023. Turkey unblocked Sweden's accession on the summit's eve, but Ukraine received no membership invitation - allies said it could not join while the war continues.

items.headline: Chandrayaan-3 launched toward the Moon
items.detail: ISRO launched Chandrayaan-3 on the LVM3 M4 rocket from Sriharikota on July 14, 2023 at 2:35 pm, carrying the Vikram lander and Pragyan rover towards a soft-landing near the lunar south pole.

items.headline: Alcaraz wins Wimbledon, ends Djokovic's reign
items.detail: Carlos Alcaraz beat defending champion Novak Djokovic in the Wimbledon men's final on July 16, 2023, while Czech Marketa Vondrousova won the women's title over Ons Jabeur. Roger Federer was honoured 20 years after his first title.

items.headline: 26 opposition parties form INDIA alliance
items.detail: Twenty-six opposition parties meeting in Bengaluru announced on July 18, 2023 that their front would be called the 'Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance' (INDIA), formed to take on the NDA in the 2024 general election.

items.headline: First co-hosted FIFA Women's World Cup kicks off
items.detail: The 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup opened on July 20, 2023 - the first edition hosted by two nations (Australia and New Zealand) and the first in the Southern Hemisphere, running to August 20.

items.headline: Israel passes 'reasonableness' law amid mass protests
items.detail: The Knesset passed the first piece of the judicial overhaul on July 24, 2023, barring the Supreme Court from striking down government decisions on 'reasonableness' grounds. The vote went 64-0 as the opposition boycotted.

items.headline: Webb telescope spots water vapour around a forming planet
items.detail: NASA announced on July 24, 2023 that the James Webb Space Telescope had detected water vapour around the young star PDS 70, where planets are forming.

items.headline: Military coup topples Niger's president
items.detail: Niger's presidential guard under General Abdourahamane Tchiani detained President Mohamed Bazoum on July 26, 2023 and seized power as the CNSP junta. ECOWAS suspended Niger, imposed sanctions and gave a one-week ultimatum to restore Bazoum, later activating a standby force.

items.headline: Lok Sabha passes Forest Conservation Amendment Bill
items.detail: The Lok Sabha passed the Forest (Conservation) Amendment Bill on July 26, 2023, permitting forest-land diversion for 'security and strategic purposes'; the Rajya Sabha cleared it on August 2.

quiz.q: Which rocket carried Chandrayaan-3 when it launched on July 14, 2023?
quiz.solution: Chandrayaan-3 flew on LVM3 M4 from Sriharikota at 2:35 pm on July 14, 2023.

quiz.q: The opposition bloc named INDIA was formed in Bengaluru with how many parties on July 18, 2023?
quiz.solution: Twenty-six parties adopted the name 'Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance'.

quiz.q: Ajit Pawar split which party when he joined the Maha Yuti alliance in July 2023?
quiz.solution: The Nationalist Congress Party split on July 2, 2023 when Ajit Pawar crossed over.

quiz.q: Who was the president ousted in Niger's July 26, 2023 coup?
quiz.solution: Presidential Guard chief Gen. Abdourahamane Tchiani detained Bazoum and formed the CNSP junta.

quiz.q: At the 2023 Vilnius summit, which country's NATO accession was unblocked by Turkey?
quiz.solution: Erdogan agreed to unblock Sweden's accession on the summit's eve.

quiz.q: Who won the 2023 Wimbledon men's singles title?
quiz.solution: Alcaraz beat defending champion Djokovic in the July 16 final.

quiz.q: Israel's July 2023 'reasonableness' law restricted the Supreme Court's power to:
quiz.solution: It bars the Court from striking down government decisions on reasonableness grounds.

quiz.q: Milan Kundera, who died in July 2023, is best known for which novel?
quiz.solution: The Czech-French writer died in Paris at 94; his 1984 novel became a modern classic.

quiz.q: The Forest Conservation (Amendment) Bill 2023 permits diversion of forest land for:
quiz.solution: The Lok Sabha passed it on July 26 and the Rajya Sabha on August 2, 2023.

quiz.q: The regional bloc that sanctioned Niger after the 2023 coup is:
quiz.solution: ECOWAS suspended Niger, imposed sanctions and gave a one-week ultimatum to restore Bazoum.

items.headline: Rajya Sabha passes Forest Conservation Amendment Bill
items.detail: The Rajya Sabha passed the Forest Conservation (Amendment) Bill on August 2, 2023, allowing diversion of forest land for 'security and strategic purposes' among other changes; the Lok Sabha had cleared it on July 26.

items.headline: Delhi services ordinance bill clears Rajya Sabha
items.detail: The Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (Amendment) Bill - replacing the May ordinance giving the central government control over Delhi bureaucrat transfers - was passed by the Rajya Sabha on August 4, 2023.

items.headline: Rahul Gandhi's Lok Sabha membership restored
items.detail: Rahul Gandhi's Wayanad Lok Sabha membership was restored on August 7, 2023, three days after the Supreme Court stayed his defamation conviction in the 'Modi surname' case, which had led to his disqualification in March.

items.headline: Maui wildfire kills over 100 in Hawaii
items.detail: A wind-driven wildfire destroyed the historic town of Lahaina on Maui, Hawaii, on August 8, 2023, killing 102 people - the deadliest US wildfire in over a century - and destroying over 2,200 structures.
examFacts: Deadliest US wildfire in a century

items.headline: Government defeats no-confidence motion
items.detail: PM Modi's government defeated the opposition's no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha by voice vote on August 10, 2023, as the opposition walked out during the debate held amid the Manipur violence discussion.

items.headline: Spain win their first FIFA Women's World Cup
items.detail: Spain beat England 1-0 in the final at Stadium Australia, Sydney on August 20, 2023 to win their first Women's World Cup. The tournament (July 20 - August 20) was the first co-hosted by two nations - Australia and New Zealand - with Aitana Bonmati winning the Golden Ball.

items.headline: BRICS invites six new members
items.detail: At the 15th BRICS Summit in Johannesburg (August 22-24, 2023), hosted by Cyril Ramaphosa, the bloc invited Argentina, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE to join from January 1, 2024.

items.headline: Chandrayaan-3 lands near the Moon's south pole
items.detail: ISRO's Vikram lander touched down near the lunar south pole at 6:04 pm IST on August 23, 2023, making India the fourth nation to soft-land on the Moon and the first ever near the south pole. The Pragyan rover rolled out to explore; the site was named Shiv Shakti Point and August 23 was declared National Space Day.
examFacts: 4th nation to soft-land; first near south pole

items.headline: Carlsen beats Praggnanandhaa to win Chess World Cup
items.detail: Magnus Carlsen defeated India's R Praggnanandhaa in the Chess World Cup final in Baku, decided in tiebreaks after the classical games were drawn, on August 24, 2023. Fabiano Caruana took third; all three qualified for the 2024 Candidates.

items.headline: Neeraj Chopra becomes world champion in javelin
items.detail: Neeraj Chopra won gold at the World Athletics Championships in Budapest with an 88.17 m javelin throw, defending his world title ahead of Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem (87.82 m). The USA topped the medal table.

items.headline: Domestic LPG cylinder price cut by Rs 200
items.detail: The government cut the price of the 14 kg domestic LPG cylinder by Rs 200 on August 29, 2023, ahead of state elections.

items.headline: Military coup in Gabon ends Bongo family rule
items.detail: Minutes after Ali Bongo was declared winner of the disputed August 26 election, General Brice Oligui Nguema seized power on August 30, 2023, ending 56 years of Bongo family rule in Gabon; the junta annulled the results.

quiz.q: On which date did Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander touch down on the Moon?
quiz.solution: The landing at 18:04 IST on August 23, 2023 is now marked as National Space Day.

quiz.q: Chandrayaan-3 was the first mission in history to soft-land near the Moon's:
quiz.solution: India became the first country to land near the lunar south pole - and the fourth to soft-land overall.

quiz.q: Which of these was NOT among the six countries invited to join BRICS at Johannesburg 2023?
quiz.solution: Argentina, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE were invited - not Indonesia.

quiz.q: The August 2023 coup in Gabon ended how many years of Bongo family rule?
quiz.solution: General Oligui Nguema's takeover ended 56 years of rule begun by Omar Bongo in 1967.

quiz.q: Who won the 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup?
quiz.solution: Spain beat England 1-0 in Sydney for a first title; Aitana Bonmati took the Golden Ball.

quiz.q: With what throw did Neeraj Chopra win gold at the 2023 World Athletics Championships?
quiz.solution: His 88.17 m beat Arshad Nadeem's 87.82 m in Budapest.

quiz.q: The August 2023 Lahaina wildfire, the deadliest in the US in over a century, struck which state?
quiz.solution: The Maui fire killed 102 people and destroyed the town of Lahaina.

quiz.q: Rahul Gandhi's Lok Sabha membership was restored in August 2023 after which court stayed his conviction?
quiz.solution: The Supreme Court stayed the 'Modi surname' defamation conviction; membership returned on August 7.

quiz.q: Who beat R Praggnanandhaa in the 2023 Chess World Cup final at Baku?
quiz.solution: Carlsen won in tiebreaks on August 24, 2023; Caruana finished third.

quiz.q: In August 2023 the government cut domestic LPG cylinder prices by:
quiz.solution: The 14 kg cylinder got a Rs 200 cut announced on August 29, 2023.

items.headline: ISRO launches Aditya-L1, its first solar mission
items.detail: ISRO launched Aditya-L1 on PSLV-C57 from Sriharikota on September 2, 2023 - India's first dedicated solar observatory, carrying seven payloads to study the photosphere, chromosphere and corona from a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange point 1.

items.headline: Deadly earthquake strikes Morocco's High Atlas
items.detail: A magnitude 6.8-6.9 earthquake struck Al Haouz province near Marrakesh on September 8, 2023, killing at least 2,960 people - Morocco's deadliest quake since the 1960 Agadir earthquake.

items.headline: India hosts the G20 New Delhi Summit
items.detail: The 18th G20 Summit - India's first - was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi on September 9-10, 2023. The New Delhi Declaration was adopted by consensus, the African Union became a permanent member, the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) was announced, and the presidency passed to Brazil under the theme 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam - One Earth, One Family, One Future'.
examFacts: Theme: One Earth, One Family, One Future

items.headline: Storm Daniel floods devastate Derna, Libya
items.detail: Storm Daniel - which first struck Greece - made landfall near Benghazi on September 10, 2023, and the next night two dams above Derna collapsed, releasing about 30 million cubic metres of water. Over 5,900 deaths were confirmed with 8,000+ missing.

items.headline: Djokovic and Gauff win the US Open
items.detail: At the US Open (August 28 - September 10, 2023), Novak Djokovic beat Daniil Medvedev in the men's final and Coco Gauff defeated Aryna Sabalenka in the women's. It was the first Grand Slam to introduce a Video Review system.

items.headline: PM Vishwakarma scheme launched for artisans
items.detail: PM Modi launched the PM Vishwakarma scheme at Coimbatore on September 17, 2023 with a Rs 13,000 crore outlay (2023-28) to support about 30 lakh artisan families with 5% collateral-free loans, toolkit e-vouchers of Rs 15,000 and training stipends.

items.headline: India crush Sri Lanka to win 8th Asia Cup
items.detail: Mohammed Siraj took 6/21 as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 50 in the Asia Cup final at Colombo on September 17, 2023; India chased 51/0 in 6.1 overs to win by 10 wickets with a record 263 balls to spare - an eighth Asia Cup title. Kuldeep Yadav was Player of the Series.

items.headline: Canada alleges Indian role in Nijjar killing; ties plummet
items.detail: On September 18, 2023, Canadian PM Justin Trudeau told Parliament that agencies were pursuing 'credible allegations' of a potential link between Indian government agents and the June 18 killing of Khalistani separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Surrey, British Columbia. Both countries expelled senior diplomats and India suspended visa services for Canadians.

items.headline: Azerbaijan's blitz ends Nagorno-Karabakh
items.detail: Azerbaijan's one-day offensive (September 19-20, 2023) forced the surrender of Nagorno-Karabakh's Armenian forces. About 100,000 ethnic Armenians - nearly the entire population - fled to Armenia, and the breakaway republic of Artsakh was dissolved by decree on September 28, 2023.

items.headline: Women's Reservation Bill passed in Parliament's special session
items.detail: During the September 18-22 special session, the Constitution (128th Amendment) Bill reserving one-third of Lok Sabha and state assembly seats for women was passed by the Lok Sabha 454-2 on September 20 and the Rajya Sabha 214-0 on September 21; the President assented on September 28 as the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act. It takes effect after a census and delimitation.

items.headline: Hangzhou Asian Games open after a year's delay
items.detail: The 19th Asian Games opened in Hangzhou, China on September 23, 2023, having been postponed from 2022 due to COVID-19. India sent 661 athletes in 35 sports and went on to a record 106-medal haul.

items.headline: NASA's OSIRIS-REx delivers asteroid samples to Earth
items.detail: NASA's OSIRIS-REx capsule landed at the Utah Test and Training Range on September 24, 2023, returning 121.6 grams of rubble from asteroid Bennu collected in 2020 - the first US asteroid sample return. The spacecraft continued on to asteroid Apophis as OSIRIS-APEX.

items.headline: FTC and states sue Amazon over monopoly allegations
items.detail: The US Federal Trade Commission and 17 states sued Amazon on September 26, 2023, alleging monopolistic practices in its marketplace.

quiz.q: Which regional bloc was admitted as a permanent G20 member at the 2023 New Delhi Summit?
quiz.solution: The African Union joined as a permanent member - the G20's first expansion since 1999.

quiz.q: The Women's Reservation Act 2023 is which Constitutional Amendment?
quiz.solution: Introduced as the 128th Amendment Bill, it became the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023.

quiz.q: Aditya-L1, launched on September 2, 2023, is India's first dedicated mission to study:
quiz.solution: Aditya-L1 is India's first dedicated solar observatory, bound for a halo orbit around L1.

quiz.q: On which date did Canada's PM Justin Trudeau make the Nijjar allegation in Parliament?
quiz.solution: Trudeau spoke in the Canadian Parliament on September 18, 2023.

quiz.q: The September 8, 2023 earthquake near Marrakesh in Morocco measured about:
quiz.solution: The Al Haouz earthquake was magnitude 6.8-6.9, Morocco's deadliest since 1960.

quiz.q: The September 2023 dam-collapse catastrophe that destroyed Derna happened in:
quiz.solution: Storm Daniel burst two dams above Derna in Libya, killing over 5,900 people.

quiz.q: How many ethnic Armenians fled Nagorno-Karabakh to Armenia after the September 2023 offensive?
quiz.solution: Roughly 100,000 - nearly the entire population - fled, and Artsakh was dissolved on September 28.

quiz.q: Who won the women's singles title at the 2023 US Open?
quiz.solution: Coco Gauff beat Sabalenka for her first Grand Slam title.

quiz.q: NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission returned samples in September 2023 from which asteroid?
quiz.solution: The capsule carried 121.6 g of material from Bennu, collected in 2020.

quiz.q: The PM Vishwakarma scheme launched in September 2023 has an outlay of:
quiz.solution: Rs 13,000 crore (2023-28) supports about 30 lakh artisan families with 5% collateral-free loans.

items.headline: Nobel Prizes 2023 announced
items.detail: The 2023 Nobels went to Katalin Kariko and Drew Weissman (Medicine, mRNA vaccines), Agostini, Krausz and L'Huillier (Physics, attosecond light pulses), Bawendi, Brus and Yekimov (Chemistry, quantum dots), Jon Fosse (Literature), Narges Mohammadi (Peace, jailed in Iran) and Claudia Goldin (Economics, women's labour market outcomes).

items.headline: Verstappen seals third straight F1 title
items.detail: Max Verstappen clinched his third Formula One World Drivers' Championship at the Qatar Grand Prix sprint in October 2023, after title rival Sergio Perez failed to finish.

items.headline: Glacial lake outburst floods Sikkim's Teesta valley
items.detail: After heavy rain, the South Lhonak glacial lake burst on October 4-5, 2023, sending a flash flood down the Teesta. The 1,200 MW Teesta III dam at Chungthang was destroyed within minutes, 15 bridges washed away and at least 92 people died.

items.headline: Cricket World Cup opens in India
items.detail: The 13th ICC Men's Cricket World Cup opened on October 5, 2023 - the first World Cup hosted solely by India - with 10 teams playing across 10 venues until November 19.
examFacts: First WC hosted solely by India

items.headline: Hamas launches surprise attack on Israel
items.detail: On October 7, 2023, Hamas' Mohammed Deif announced 'Operation Al-Aqsa Flood': over 3,500 rockets were fired while fighters breached the Gaza barrier and attacked at least 22 locations in southern Israel, killing hundreds and taking scores hostage. Israel formally declared war in response.

items.headline: India's best-ever Asian Games: 106 medals
items.detail: India finished the Hangzhou Asian Games (September 23 - October 8, 2023) with a best-ever 106 medals - 28 gold, 38 silver, 40 bronze - ranking fourth and becoming only the fourth nation to cross 100 medals at one Asiad. Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty won India's first Asiad badminton gold; shooting led with 22 medals.

items.headline: Herat earthquakes kill over 2,400 in Afghanistan
items.detail: Two magnitude 6.3 earthquakes struck Afghanistan's Herat province on October 7-8, 2023, killing at least 2,445 people and injuring over 9,000.

items.headline: Australia rejects Indigenous Voice referendum
items.detail: Australian voters rejected the October 14, 2023 referendum that would have created an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander 'Voice to Parliament', a constitutional advisory body for Indigenous Australians.

items.headline: New Zealand elects Luxon's National Party
items.detail: In New Zealand's October 14, 2023 election the opposition National Party won the most seats, with Christopher Luxon set to form a coalition with ACT New Zealand, ending Labour's six years under Chris Hipkins and Jacinda Ardern.

items.headline: 'Ring of fire' eclipse crosses the Americas
items.detail: An annular solar eclipse - the 'ring of fire' - was visible across the Western Hemisphere on October 14, 2023, tracking from the US through Central and South America.

items.headline: Cricket approved for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics
items.detail: Cricket returned to the Olympic programme after 128 years when the 141st IOC Session in Mumbai confirmed it for LA 2028 on October 16, 2023 - T20 format with six teams each in men's and women's events. Cricket's only earlier Olympic appearance was in 1900.

items.headline: Supreme Court declines to legalise same-sex marriage
items.detail: A five-judge Constitution bench headed by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud ruled on October 17, 2023 that there is no fundamental right to marry and left the question of same-sex marriage to Parliament and state legislatures.

items.headline: ISRO tests Gaganyaan crew escape system
items.detail: ISRO's TV-D1 Test Vehicle Development flight on October 21, 2023 demonstrated the Gaganyaan Crew Escape System - the rocket aborted at Mach 1.2 at altitude, the crew module separated, splashed into the Bay of Bengal and was recovered by the Indian Navy.

items.headline: Mike Johnson becomes US House Speaker
items.detail: Louisiana Republican Mike Johnson was elected Speaker of the US House of Representatives on October 25, 2023, ending three weeks of deadlock after Kevin McCarthy's removal.

items.headline: India's best-ever Asian Para Games
items.detail: India returned from the Hangzhou Asian Para Games (October 22-28, 2023) with a best-ever 108 medals - 27 gold, 32 silver, 49 bronze - finishing sixth in the standings.

items.headline: MY Bharat youth platform launched on Unity Day
items.detail: PM Modi launched 'Mera Yuva Bharat' (MY Bharat) at Kartavya Path on October 31, 2023 - National Unity Day, Sardar Patel's birth anniversary. The phygital platform for Indians aged 15-29 aims at youth-led development towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

quiz.q: What was the name of Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack on Israel?
quiz.solution: Hamas commander Mohammed Deif announced it as 'Operation Al-Aqsa Flood'; Israel then declared war.

quiz.q: At which IOC Session was cricket confirmed for the 2028 Olympics?
quiz.solution: The 141st IOC Session in Mumbai approved cricket on October 16, 2023 - T20, six teams per gender.

quiz.q: How many medals did India win at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games - its best-ever haul?
quiz.solution: India won 106 medals (28 gold), ranking 4th and crossing 100 medals for the first time.

quiz.q: In its October 17, 2023 verdict, the Supreme Court on same-sex marriage:
options: Referred it to a larger bench indefinitely
quiz.solution: The 5-judge bench held there is no fundamental right to marry and left the issue to legislatures.

quiz.q: ISRO's October 2023 TV-D1 flight test demonstrated the:
quiz.solution: The high-altitude abort test validated separation of the Gaganyaan Crew Escape System.

quiz.q: Who won the 2023 Nobel Peace Prize?
quiz.solution: The jailed Iranian activist won for her fight against the oppression of women in Iran.

quiz.q: Australia's October 14, 2023 referendum on the Indigenous 'Voice to Parliament' was:
options: Passed with a record yes vote
quiz.solution: A majority of Australians voted against creating the constitutional advisory body.

quiz.q: Who was elected Speaker of the US House of Representatives on October 25, 2023?
quiz.solution: Louisiana's Mike Johnson ended three weeks of deadlock after McCarthy's removal.

quiz.q: Which dam was destroyed by the October 2023 glacial-lake flood in Sikkim?
quiz.solution: The 1,200 MW Teesta III dam was destroyed within minutes by the South Lhonak lake outburst.

quiz.q: MY Bharat (Mera Yuva Bharat) was launched by the PM on National Unity Day 2023 for youth in which age group?
quiz.solution: The phygital platform targets Indians aged 15-29, launched on Sardar Patel's birth anniversary.

items.headline: Assembly elections held in five states
items.detail: Polling for five state assemblies took place in November 2023 - Mizoram (Nov 7), Chhattisgarh (Nov 7 and 17), Madhya Pradesh (Nov 17), Rajasthan (Nov 25) and Telangana (Nov 30) - with counting on December 3.
examFacts: 5 states: Mizoram, Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Telangana

items.headline: Silkyara tunnel collapse; all 41 workers rescued
items.detail: A 60-metre section of the Silkyara Bend-Barkot tunnel on the Char Dham road project in Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand collapsed on November 12, 2023, trapping 41 workers. After about two weeks, all were rescued on November 28 using an escape pipe, with manual 'rat-hole' miners clearing the last stretch.

items.headline: Biden and Xi meet at APEC in San Francisco
items.detail: US President Joe Biden and China's Xi Jinping held talks in San Francisco on the sidelines of the APEC summit on November 15, 2023 - their first meeting in over a year - with progress reported on drug trafficking and AI cooperation.
examFacts: First Biden-Xi talks in a year

items.headline: UK Supreme Court rules Rwanda asylum plan unlawful
items.detail: The UK Supreme Court unanimously held on November 15, 2023 that the government's plan to send asylum seekers to Rwanda was unlawful, saying Rwanda could not be treated as a safe third country.
examFacts: Scheme later revived by the Safety of Rwanda Act

items.headline: Bangladesh poll date set for January 7
items.detail: Bangladesh's Election Commission announced parliamentary elections for January 7, 2024, after weeks of opposition protests demanding a caretaker government.

items.headline: Kohli breaks Tendulkar's record with 50th ODI century
items.detail: Virat Kohli scored his 50th One-Day International century during the 2023 World Cup, surpassing Sachin Tendulkar's long-standing record of 49. Kohli finished the tournament as Player of the Tournament with a record 765 runs.

items.headline: Mohamed Muizzu sworn in as Maldives president
items.detail: Mohamed Muizzu of the People's National Congress was sworn in as the 8th President of the Maldives on November 17, 2023, having beaten incumbent Ibrahim Mohamed Solih with 54.04% in the September 30 runoff. Hussain Mohamed Latheef became vice president.

items.headline: OpenAI board fires Sam Altman; he returns within days
items.detail: OpenAI's board removed CEO Sam Altman on November 17, 2023, with Mira Murati named interim CEO and president Greg Brockman resigning. After about 95% of employees threatened to quit, Altman was reinstated within a week.

items.headline: Nicaragua's Sheynnis Palacios wins Miss Universe
items.detail: Sheynnis Palacios of Nicaragua won Miss Universe 2023 at San Salvador, El Salvador on November 18, 2023 - her country's first win in the pageant's history. Thailand's Anntonia Porsild was first runner-up among 84 delegates; India's Shweta Sharda reached the Top 20.

items.headline: Milei wins Argentina's presidential runoff
items.detail: Libertarian outsider Javier Milei won Argentina's presidential runoff on November 19, 2023, defeating economy minister Sergio Massa by about 56% to 44%.

items.headline: Australia beat India to win a sixth Cricket World Cup
items.detail: Australia defeated hosts India by six wickets in the final at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad on November 19, 2023, winning a record sixth World Cup. Mohammed Shami was the leading wicket-taker with 24 scalps in a tournament India had entered the final unbeaten.

items.headline: Djokovic claims record 7th ATP Finals title
items.detail: Novak Djokovic beat Italy's Jannik Sinner 6-3, 6-3 in the ATP Finals championship match to win a record seventh season-ending title, moving past Roger Federer's six.

items.headline: Wilders' party wins most seats in Dutch election
items.detail: Geert Wilders' far-right Party for Freedom (PVV) won the most seats in the November 22, 2023 Dutch general election for all 150 seats of the House of Representatives, upending Dutch politics.

items.headline: Israel Cabinet approves temporary Gaza ceasefire
items.detail: Israel's Cabinet approved a four-day ceasefire in Gaza on November 22, 2023, brokered by Egypt, Qatar and the US, under which Israel would free 150 Palestinian prisoners in exchange for hostages held by Hamas.

items.headline: Justice M. Fathima Beevi, first woman Supreme Court judge, dies
items.detail: Justice M. Fathima Beevi, the first woman appointed to the Supreme Court of India (1989) and a former Governor of Tamil Nadu, died on November 23, 2023, aged 96.

items.headline: Government signs peace pact with Manipur's UNLF
items.detail: The Centre signed a peace agreement with the United National Liberation Front (UNLF) on November 29, 2023 - described as the oldest Meitei insurgent group in Manipur.

quiz.q: Who won the 2023 Men's Cricket World Cup, held in India?
quiz.solution: Australia beat India by six wickets in the Ahmedabad final for a record sixth title.

quiz.q: Whose record of 49 ODI centuries did Virat Kohli surpass during the 2023 World Cup?
quiz.solution: Kohli's 50th ODI hundred went past Sachin Tendulkar's long-standing 49.

quiz.q: The Silkyara tunnel where 41 workers were trapped in November 2023 is part of which project?
quiz.solution: The Silkyara Bend-Barkot tunnel in Uttarkashi belongs to the Char Dham project; all 41 were rescued on November 28.

quiz.q: Justice M. Fathima Beevi, who died in November 2023, was the first woman:
options: Judge of the Supreme Court of India
Chief Justice of a High Court
quiz.solution: She became the first woman Supreme Court judge in 1989 and later Governor of Tamil Nadu.

quiz.q: Mohamed Muizzu, sworn in as president in November 2023, leads which country?
quiz.solution: He became the 8th President of the Maldives on November 17, 2023, defeating Ibrahim Mohamed Solih.

quiz.q: Which company's board fired CEO Sam Altman on November 17, 2023, only to reinstate him days later?
quiz.solution: OpenAI's board removed Altman; after mass employee protest he returned within a week.

quiz.q: Which party won the most seats in the November 2023 Dutch general election?
quiz.solution: Geert Wilders' PVV emerged as the largest party in the 150-seat House.

quiz.q: Sheynnis Palacios, who won Miss Universe 2023, gave which country its first-ever title?
quiz.solution: Nicaragua's Palacios won in San Salvador; Thailand's Anntonia Porsild was runner-up.

quiz.q: With roughly what vote share did Javier Milei win Argentina's November 2023 runoff?
quiz.solution: Milei beat Sergio Massa about 56% to 44% before taking office on December 10.

quiz.q: In November 2023 the Centre signed a peace agreement with UNLF, an insurgent group of which state?
quiz.solution: UNLF is described as the oldest Meitei insurgent group in Manipur; the pact was signed on November 29.

items.headline: BJP wins three of five state elections
items.detail: Results declared on December 3-4, 2023 gave the BJP wins in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, the Congress won Telangana, and the Zoram People's Movement won Mizoram.

items.headline: Cyclone Michaung batters Chennai and Andhra coast
items.detail: Cyclone Michaung made landfall near Bapatla on the Andhra Pradesh coast on December 5, 2023 after lashing Chennai with over 530 mm of rain. At least 17 people died, Chennai airport shut and Tamil Nadu suffered over Rs 11,000 crore in losses.

items.headline: EU negotiators strike world's first AI law deal
items.detail: European Parliament and Council negotiators agreed on December 9, 2023 on the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, the world's first comprehensive, risk-based AI law. Parliament formally adopted it in March 2024.

items.headline: Javier Milei sworn in as Argentina's president
items.detail: Libertarian economist Javier Milei, who won the November 19 runoff, was sworn in as President of Argentina on December 10, 2023, succeeding Alberto Fernandez.

items.headline: Supreme Court upholds Article 370 abrogation
items.detail: A five-judge Constitution bench of the Supreme Court unanimously upheld the constitutionality of the abrogation of Article 370 on December 11, 2023, dismissing 23 petitions against the 2019 decision that ended Jammu and Kashmir's special status.

items.headline: Security breach in Lok Sabha chamber
items.detail: On the 22nd anniversary of the 2001 Parliament attack, two people jumped into the Lok Sabha chamber from the visitors' gallery and released yellow smoke canisters on December 13, 2023; two others were detained outside. Fourteen MPs were suspended the next day over related protests.

items.headline: COP28 ends with first call to move away from fossil fuels
items.detail: The COP28 summit in Dubai (November 30 to December 13, 2023) adopted the 'UAE Consensus' - the first COP pact to call for 'transitioning away from fossil fuels' - and a Loss and Damage fund operationalised on day one.
examFacts: Loss and Damage fund on day one

items.headline: Surat Diamond Bourse opens as world's largest office building
items.detail: PM Modi inaugurated the Surat Diamond Bourse in Gujarat on December 17, 2023. The 660,000 sq m complex of nine towers is certified by Guinness as the world's largest office building, surpassing the Pentagon.

items.headline: 141 MPs suspended in Parliament breach aftermath
items.detail: Parliament suspended 49 more Lok Sabha MPs on December 19, 2023 over protests demanding action on the security breach, taking total suspensions to 141 - the highest in a single session.
examFacts: 95 from Lok Sabha, 46 from Rajya Sabha

items.headline: Mitchell Starc becomes IPL's costliest buy in Dubai auction
items.detail: At the IPL 2024 auction - the first ever held abroad, in Dubai - Mitchell Starc became the most expensive player in IPL history at Rs 24.75 crore to Kolkata Knight Riders, and Pat Cummins went for Rs 20.5 crore to Sunrisers Hyderabad.

items.headline: Government suspends newly elected WFI body
items.detail: The Sports Ministry suspended the newly elected Wrestling Federation of India executive on December 24, 2023 - days after Sanjay Singh, an ally of former chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, won the presidency - and handed charge to an IOA ad-hoc committee.

items.headline: INS Imphal commissioned into the Navy
items.detail: The stealth guided-missile destroyer INS Imphal was commissioned at Mumbai on December 26, 2023 in the presence of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The Rs 8,950 crore Project 15B ship is the first named after a city in Northeast India.

items.headline: South Africa win Centurion Test by an innings
items.detail: South Africa beat India by an innings and 32 runs in the first Test at Centurion (December 26-29, 2023), taking the lead in a series later drawn 1-1.
examFacts: SA won by an innings and 32 runs

items.headline: Tamil actor-politician Vijayakanth dies at 71
items.detail: Vijayakanth - 'Captain' of Tamil cinema with 154 films and founder of the Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK), a former Leader of the Opposition in Tamil Nadu - died in Chennai on December 28, 2023. He was given the Padma Bhushan posthumously.

items.headline: PM inaugurates Ayodhya airport ahead of Ram Mandir
items.detail: PM Modi inaugurated the Maharishi Valmiki International Airport at Ayodhya on December 30, 2023, weeks before the Ram Mandir consecration; commercial flights began on January 10, 2024.

quiz.q: In the December 2023 state elections, the BJP won which set of states?
quiz.solution: The BJP took Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh; Congress won only Telangana; ZPM won Mizoram.

quiz.q: On December 11, 2023, the Supreme Court upheld:
quiz.solution: A five-judge bench unanimously upheld the 2019 abrogation of Article 370.

quiz.q: The December 13, 2023 Parliament security breach happened on the anniversary of:
quiz.solution: The breach occurred on the 22nd anniversary of the 2001 Parliament attack.

quiz.q: The COP28 'UAE Consensus' was the first COP pact to call for:
quiz.solution: COP28 in Dubai (Nov 30 - Dec 13, 2023) first called for 'transitioning away from fossil fuels'.

quiz.q: Which bowler became the costliest buy in IPL history at the December 2023 auction?
quiz.solution: Starc went to KKR for Rs 24.75 crore at the Dubai auction; Cummins fetched Rs 20.5 crore.

quiz.q: INS Imphal, commissioned in December 2023, is notable as the first Indian Navy ship named after:
quiz.solution: The Project 15B destroyer is the first named after a Northeast Indian city.

quiz.q: Javier Milei was sworn in as president of which country in December 2023?
quiz.solution: The libertarian outsider won the runoff on November 19 and took office on December 10, 2023.

quiz.q: Cyclone Michaung, which flooded Chennai in December 2023, made landfall in:
quiz.solution: It made landfall near Bapatla on the Andhra Pradesh coast on December 5, 2023.

quiz.q: The Surat Diamond Bourse, inaugurated in December 2023, is certified as:
quiz.solution: The 660,000 sq m, nine-tower complex surpassed the Pentagon per Guinness World Records.

quiz.q: Vijayakanth, who died in December 2023, founded which party?
quiz.solution: He founded the DMDK in 2005 and served as Tamil Nadu's Leader of the Opposition.
